intro: Lesson 32: Group 7 and Group 0. To understand the properties and uses of the halogens and the noble gases

questions.q: Chlorine water is added to potassium iodide. What happens and why?
questions.a: Iodine is displaced (solution turns brown) because chlorine is more reactive than iodine
questions.model: Compare reactivity: chlorine is higher up Group 7, so more reactive. More reactive displaces less reactive. So iodine is pushed out: brown colour.

questions.q: Why is helium used in balloons?
questions.a: It is less dense than air and unreactive (not flammable)

questions.q: Name the state of chlorine at room temperature.
Complete the displacement grid on the sheet (Cl, Br, I with chloride, bromide, iodide solutions): tick where a reaction happens and write one word equation.
questions.a: Reactions: Cl with bromide and iodide; Br with iodide only; I with none
questions.model: Teacher fills the chlorine row on screen.

questions.q: Why were noble gases the last group to be discovered?
questions.a: They are unreactive, colourless gases, so they do not form compounds that would reveal them.

questions.q: Big question: why is a little chlorine added to water?
questions.a: It kills harmful microorganisms in tiny, safe amounts.
